Assume that a zero-coupon bond that pays 1 at time $T$ has price $p(t,T)$
contracted at time $t$. Naturally, for all $t$, $p(t,t)=1$ and $p(t,T)$ is
well-defined for all $t\in \mathbb{R}$. Assume that $p(t,T)$ is also
well-defined for all $T\in \mathbb{R}$ and is differentiable w.r.t $T$.  

If the accumulation of interest can be described by a constant continuous-time
interest rate on $[t,T]$ denoted $y(t,T)$, then
$$
p(t,T)e^{y(t,T)(T-t)}=1,
$$
solves
$$
y(t,T)=- \frac{1}{T-t}\log p(t,T),
$$
called the **yield curve** viewed as a function in $T$ after fixing $t$.
